dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL with SCREEN SECTION, UNSIGNED-INT, FOREGROUND-COLOR, REVERSE-VIDEO, BLINK — typical GnuCOBOL terminal/screen application. Uses FUNCTION in REPOSITORY clause and 88-level condition names extensively.
evidence: SCREEN SECTION with FOREGROUND-COLOR, REVERSE-VIDEO, BLINK, HIGHLIGHT

purpose.domain_detail: Multi-feature terminal application called 'Vault' with login/registration, library, arcade games (Hangman, Tic-Tac-Toe, random number guessing), message board, credits/banking system, and about pages — themed after Fallout's Pip-Boy
purpose.summary: A large GnuCOBOL terminal application named 'server' that implements a multi-menu system with user authentication, a virtual library, arcade games (Hangman, Tic-Tac-Toe), a message board, a credit/currency system, and an about section. The UI is styled after the Fallout video game Pip-Boy device with ASCII art. It reads/writes multiple flat files for persistence.

notable_features: SCREEN SECTION with full-screen TUI layout
REPOSITORY clause with user-defined FUNCTION declarations
OCCURS DEPENDING ON for variable-length tables
ASCENDING KEY with INDEXED BY for sorted tables
88-level condition names for game state management
ASCII art Pip-Boy display in SCREEN SECTION
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
verdict.notes: Source truncated to first 16000 chars; full program is 2410 lines. The program appears to be a student or hobbyist project of substantial size, well-structured with multiple divisions and features. The Pip-Boy theming and game features suggest a creative/portfolio project rather than commercial production code, but it is complex enough to be classified as production-like in terms of COBOL craftsmanship.
